```python
def longest_palindromic_substring(s: str) -> str:
    """Return the longest contiguous substring of s that is a palindrome.

    Uses expand-around-center in O(n^2) time and O(1) extra space, checking
    both odd and even length centers.
    """
    if not s:
        return ""

    best_l = best_r = 0

    def expand(left: int, right: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
        while left >= 0 and right < len(s) and s[left] == s[right]:
            left -= 1
            right += 1
        return left + 1, right - 1

    for i in range(len(s)):
        for l, r in (expand(i, i), expand(i, i + 1)):
            if r - l > best_r - best_l:
                best_l, best_r = l, r
    return s[best_l:best_r + 1]
```

The algorithm treats each character and each gap between characters as a possible palindrome center. A palindrome can be extended only while the two boundary characters match, so every expansion is linear in the worst case and there are O(n) centers, giving O(n²) time.
